items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: I understand in a certain sense why Art Blakey had — well from my perspective, not from Art Blakey’s — when he started to hire younger musicians.

ctx.x: Have you noticed, we also had talked a little bit about people’s attention span. And this was ten years ago. And now things have — the demands on our attention, multi-tasking etcetera, have greatly increased. Does that affect your audience do you think? Are they affected by that?

Well you’re interviewing me. I can’t lay out this long history. Because history is not sexy. And we had spoke about Malcolm Gladwell’s A Tipping Point. There has to be a stickiness. And you have to sort of go for it, and then we are also living in a highly competitive economic society and people don’t have the time, they’re overscheduled and you really have to like — it’s almost like being in New York in the zoo. You’ve got to — no matter if you lay out your best shot, it may not be embraced, you may not get that…
What did Max Roach have that was unique? What was unique about Max Roach?
